keys.warmupRoutine_v1:
"VITAMINS - EVERY SINGLE DAY
The floor you never drop below. Not a workout - the thing that makes the workout possible.
No standards, no scoring, no skipping. If you are in the gym, this happened.
About 20 minutes. Same order every day so you never think about it.

HANDLING - stationary, both hands, eyes up the whole time
1 high 1 low
rapid switch
low around the leg
under the low arm
hi ho
figure 8

HANDLING - on the move
skips through and backwards
lowmans
misdirection through and behind

TOUCH AT THE RIM
Regular mikans
Wide 1 foot mikans
Spin mikans high and low
Spin mikans 1 side
Floaters around the arc

VITAMINS PROPER - your daily dose of counters
Killer cross to burnsey
In and out to spin layup
Reverse through to euro

FORM
5 one-hand form shots, each hand

JUMP TOUCH - Pickens series
5 Pickens 3 jumps
5 Pickens 1 leg
5 Pickens side jump
5 Pickens lateral bound
5 Pickens jump backs
5 Pickens three through pickups

CLOSE
10 one leg chair
10 chair high arcs
10 threes, then free throws to leave

WHAT CHANGED FROM YOUR OLD WARMUP
Nothing was removed. It was one long list and is now grouped by what each part is for, so a day
you are short on time you cut a GROUP, not a random line. If you have to cut, cut Jump Touch -
it is the one thing your lift already covers."

Read this once. It turns the one number you already produce every day into a real one.

WHEN
End of the afternoon block, both halves, back to back. Shooting them tired is the better rep and
it means you log the whole day in one moment instead of carrying a number around since morning.

THE 50 THREES - 5 racks of 10, always these spots, always this order
1. Right corner - 10
2. Right wing - 10
3. Top of the key - 10
4. Left wing - 10
5. Left corner - 10
Type each rack the second it ends. Five small numbers beat one number at the end.
WHY THIS MATTERS: without fixed spots, 34/50 from the corners and 34/50 from the top look identical
in your log and they are not the same day. Undefined spots are why the number never meant anything.

THE 50 FREE THROWS - 5 sets of 10
Sets of 10 only so you never have to hold a count past ten.

LOG IT
One row in the Log table: date, threes out of 50, free throws out of 50.
78 rows exist and at six days a week they run out in mid-November. Add more before the season.

WHAT A GOOD DAY IS
You do not know yet, and that is the point. Shoot it for ten days, then your line gets set from
your own numbers rather than from a guess. Until then the only job is putting a row in the table."},{"title":"Log","type":"table","columns":["Date","Threes/50","Free Throws/50"],"rows":[["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""],["","",""]]}]},"4":{"sel":0,"pages":[{"title":"Conditioning","body":"AEROBIC

Attach this to the END of your bag work, twice a week. It is a finisher, not a session.
Games are played tired. Every other skill block in your program is done fresh.
Pick one and rotate. About 10 minutes.

1. MAKE OR REPEAT
Pick a bag package. You do not leave a drill until you hit its written standard.
Miss the standard and the whole drill runs again. No partial credit.

2. SHOOTING ON EMPTY
Sprint the floor twice, then shoot 5 from the wing. Five rounds.
Track makes out of 25. This is the honest number, not your fresh one.

3. FREE THROWS TIRED
Every time you finish a hard block anywhere in your day, shoot 2 free throws before you sit down.
Log makes out of the day's total attempts.

4. BEAT THE CLOCK
Shot clock on your phone. 30 seconds to get a specific shot off a specific action.
10 rounds. Do not get the shot off and it counts as a miss.

5. ONE MINUTE SPOTS
60 seconds at one spot, as many makes as you can. Rest 60. Five spots.
Log total makes and compare month to month.

LOG IT - here, overwrite it each time
LAST RUN: drill ___   number ___   date ___
The number here will always be worse than your fresh number. That is the point.
When the gap between tired and fresh shrinks, you are actually getting somewhere."}]},"5":{"sel":0,"pages":[{"title":"Partner Menu","body":"PARTNER MENU
Grab one of these when somebody is in the gym with you. 20 minutes, zero planning.
This REPLACES the passing block that day. Live reads beat wall reps every time.
Pick by what you have not done recently, not by what you feel like doing.

1. LIVE PASSING READS - 20 min
He plays help off your drive. He commits or he does not and you read it.
Drive and read 6x ea side, then ball screen with him as the coverage 10x ea side.
The only rule: he never tells you what he is doing beforehand.

2. ONE ON ONE, FULL - 20 min
Live, both ends. First to 7, win by 2. Write the score down.
Pick what you are hunting before you start, same as a practice intention.

3. CLOSEOUT AND CONTAIN, LIVE - 20 min
He starts with the ball on the wing, you start under the rim. You close, he attacks.
6 reps then switch. You win the rep if he never gets a straight-line drive.

4. SCREEN NAVIGATION, LIVE - 20 min
He comes off a screen you have to get through. Over, under, or top lock - call it before the rep.
8 reps ea side then switch.

5. CONTESTED SHOOTING - 20 min
He closes out for real, you shoot for real. 20 off the catch, 20 off the dribble.
Track makes. Compare it to your 50/50 number - the gap is what pressure costs you.

6. REBOUNDING AND BOX OUT - 20 min
Live box out off a shot. First to 10 rebounds.
The most under-trained thing a guard can do with a partner.

LOG IT - here, overwrite it each time
LAST RUN: drill ___   score ___   date ___
If you have not run one of these in three weeks, that is the one you do next."},{"title":"Practice Intentions","body":"PRACTICE INTENTIONS
Live reps without a target are just cardio. Pick ONE before every practice and every run.
One. Not three. You cannot hunt three things at once and you will end up hunting none.
Write it on the line below before you go, and score yourself out of 10 after.
TODAY: ___                                 AFTER: ___ /10
LAST PRACTICE: ___                         ___ /10

DEFENSE
I do not get beat baseline once.
I get over every ball screen. No going under unless I call it first.
I am in a stance before he catches, not after.
I finish possessions - I box out every single time a shot goes up.
I talk on every screen. Every one.

PASSING AND DECISIONS
I hit the roller at least three times.
I make the extra pass every time I am two feet from a good shot and someone has a better one.
Zero live-dribble turnovers.
I look weak side before I pick up my dribble.
I throw at least one skip pass.

SCORING
I get to a left-hand finish twice.
No contested twos.
I shoot every open catch-and-shoot without hesitating.
I get downhill off the first side action instead of the third.

MOVEMENT AND COMPETE
I sprint the floor both ways every possession of one full drill.
My hips stay low through every screen I navigate.
I stop on one step, not three.

HOW TO USE IT
Rotate through them. Do not repeat one until you have scored yourself 8 or better on it twice.
A 4 out of 10 is more useful than a 9 - it tells you what to hunt next time.
The point is not the score. The point is that you walked in looking for something."},{"title":"NERVOUS SYSTEM - Hot and Cold","body":"NERVOUS SYSTEM - HOT AND COLD
The mental side. Not reads, not IQ. The piece that decides whether the skills you built show up.
Written after the first practice with the new team: nervous walking in, mistakes compounding,
playing to not mess up, body gone weak. Hot first, then cold. This page is the tool for both.
Nothing here is scored, levelled or laddered. Confidence is not a drill. It is what evidence
leaves behind, and the only job of this page is to keep you doing things that produce evidence.

THE LOOP - why it went the way it went
Nerves put the body in a threat state. Under threat the body protects, it does not perform.
That is the weakness you felt.
With nothing specific to hunt, "don't mess up" filled the empty slot.
Avoidance goals make you slow, because every option gets risk-checked before you act.
Slow is what produces the mistakes. Each one confirms the threat. Round it goes.
The fix is not feeling more confident. It is: bring the body down a notch, fill the slot, and
cut the loop after every mistake so nothing compounds. Three tools, one each.

THE TWO BREATHS - opposite jobs, do not mix them up
DOWN  Two inhales through the nose - a full one, then a short top-up on top of it - then one long
      slow exhale through the mouth until you are empty. One of these drops arousal faster than
      anything else you can do on purpose. In a practice or a game, one to three. Five minutes of
      it is the morning practice.
UP    Short sharp inhales through the nose, quick exhale, and MOVE - sprint, jump, slap the floor.
      For when you have gone flat. It is the opposite tool.

DAILY - trains the reflex so it is there when you need it. No new time.
MORNING  Your "Meditate 5 minutes" slot. Five minutes of DOWN breaths, one after another, sitting
         up, eyes closed. That is the whole practice. You are grooving the exact breath you will
         use walking into the gym, so it works without thinking when your hands are shaking.
NIGHT    Your "Slow Breathe" line. In through the nose 4 seconds, out through the nose 6, five
         minutes, lying down. Longer out than in - that is the only rule.
GYM      The reset below runs after every miss in 50/50 and every wrong read in Reads. Dozens of
         free reps a day of the thing that stops mistakes compounding, in a place where a miss
         costs nothing.

BEFORE - walking in
The target is not calm. Calm is flat and flat gets beat. The target is ready without threat:
same heart rate, no danger in it.
1. Three DOWN breaths on the walk in. Takes the top off. Does not take you to zero.
2. Say the intention out loud. ONE, off the Practice Intentions page, chosen before you left the
   room. Now the slot is full and "don't mess up" has nowhere to sit.
3. First possession is an effort job - sprint the floor, hit somebody on a screen, talk. Something
   you cannot fail. You are in the practice before the ball has touched your hands.
Nerves and excitement are the same body. The only difference is the label you put on it. When you
feel it: "that is the body getting ready". Never "calm down" - it does not work, and it tells
you something is wrong.

BETWEEN - the reset, after every mistake, 3 seconds
Mistakes are not the problem. Carrying one into the next possession is.
The reset is physical so it does not need a thought you might not have in you:
  1. One physical cue. Wipe your hands on your shorts, or pull the jersey. Same one every time.
  2. One DOWN breath.
  3. Eyes up to the next thing - the ball, or your man's chest. Find your job.
Done. You do not review the mistake. You do not get to review it until film.
Same reset after a good play. A good play you are still thinking about is the next mistake.
This is what you groove in the gym. By the time it matters it is not a decision, it is a habit.

GONE COLD - the opposite of everything above
You will know it: passing up open shots, body heavy, hoping the play goes somewhere else. That is
the freeze branch. Slow breathing sinks you further. Do not use it here.
1. UP breaths. Two or three sharp ones, and move - sprint to your spot on the next dead ball.
2. Eyes OUT. At the rim, at his chest, at the ball. Not inward. Cold lives inside your head.
3. Voice. Call every screen, every switch, every get-back, loud. Talking is a job you cannot
   fail and it drags your attention back onto the game.
4. One effort goal for the next three possessions that skill cannot ruin: sprint both ways, box
   out every shot, get a deflection. Effort still works when skill is gone, and every one you
   finish is a piece of evidence. Evidence is the only thing confidence is made of.
An open shot is still shot. Hesitating on it is the symptom, not a fix. Shoot it and reset.

WHAT THIS IS NOT
Not a confidence ladder. Not a mood score. Not a page you level up. The only measure is whether
the tools got used, and that is yes or no.
LAST PRACTICE: walked in with the slot full? ___   reset after mistakes? ___   went cold? ___

WHEN IT IS BIGGER THAN A PAGE
If it gets to where it got - the panic, the body shutting down - and it happens again, that is a
recurring thing worth taking to somebody. CWRU counselling is free and a sports psych is standard
equipment at the level you are chasing. It is a tool, same as a lift."},{"title":"Film + IQ","body":"FILM + IQ
10 minutes, off court, in the evening. Costs you no gym time at all.
This is the cheapest development available to you and the one almost every player skips.
Rotation: A, B, C, D. Check the LAST RUN line.
LAST RUN: ___ (A, B, C or D)   date ___

BLOCK A - YOUR OWN GAME FILM - 10 min
Watch your own possessions from practice or a run, whatever you can get.
Count three things and write the numbers here: live-dribble turnovers, times a better pass was
open and you shot instead, and times you got beat off the dribble.
LAST COUNT: turnovers ___   passed-up ___   beaten ___
Do not watch for highlights. You already know what your good plays looked like.

BLOCK B - READ THE COVERAGE - 10 min
Pull up any college or NBA game. Watch nothing but ball screens.
Before the ball handler acts, PAUSE and call it out loud: over, under, switch, drop, hedge.
Then play it and see what the defense actually did and what he did about it.
20 reps. You are training the read, not the move.

BLOCK C - STUDY A GUARD - 10 min
Pick one guard built like you who plays your role. Watch one game a week of him and only him.
Watch what he does WITHOUT the ball and how he gets the ball where he wants it.
Steal one specific thing, write it down, take it into the gym that week.

BLOCK D - YOUR TEAM'S ACTIONS - 10 min
Know your own playbook cold. Every action, every counter, every spot you occupy.
The fastest way onto the floor as a freshman is being the guy who never blows the play.
Write out one action from memory. If you cannot, that is the one you study tomorrow.

FILM CHECK
Once the movement analysis is built, Block A becomes the slot where your own movement clips get
reviewed alongside your game possessions. Capture per the Film Protocol page in Court movement.

PROGRESSION
Overwrite the LAST RUN line. Streak beats depth here - ten minutes four times a week beats an hour once.
Block A: those three numbers should trend down over a month. That is the entire measure.
Block B: progress by calling the read EARLIER - before the screen is set instead of after."},{"title":"PRACTICE - TRANSITION AND READS","body":"PRACTICE - TRANSITION AND READS

Read this before practice. Pick two. Not five, two. Score yourself out of 10 after, on the line below.
PICKED: ___ and ___          AFTER: ___ /10 and ___ /10

This page exists because these are the things that cannot be repped alone. Reps Transition grooves the movement. This is where the deciding gets trained, and Tuesday is the only day it can happen.

TRANSITION OFFENSE
First look is up the floor on every rebound and every make, before the ball goes down. Count the possessions I looked first.
Push past the free throw line before I decide anything. No decision made above the arc.
Name the advantage to myself every break. Numbers, mismatch, or none. If none, pull it out on the first beat instead of driving into a set defense.
Every break ends one of three ways. I finish it, I hit the man ahead, or I pull it out clean. No dead dribble in the middle third.
When I am not the ball, I run wide to the corner every time. No drifting to the wing early.
As the trail man I am ready before the catch, and I shoot it in one motion if it is there.

TRANSITION DEFENSE
Paint first, man second. Get to the paint, then find who I have.
I take the most dangerous man, not my man, until we are matched up.
I talk on every get back. Call the ball, call who I have, out loud, every possession.
My first step after my own shot is back. Count the possessions I lost that step.

READING A CLOSEOUT
Three options on the catch and I decide on the catch, not before it. Shoot it. Attack the high shoulder. One more, and relocate.

BALL SCREEN, THE LATE READ
I do not decide before I leave. I read the coverage after the first dribble, not at the point of the screen. If I know the answer before I come off it, that was a bag rep, not a live one.
Hedge and blitz are the two coverages I have never repped anywhere. Those are the ones to go looking for at practice."},{"title":"GROUP WORKOUT IDEAS - parked","body":"GROUP WORKOUT IDEAS - PARKED
Everything that needs a body. Nothing here is scheduled. We look at this after the solo system
is finished.

WHY THIS PAGE EXISTS
Contact and physicality came out of every solo page on purpose. A wall does not move, does not
recover, and does not push back - training contact against one teaches you to lean, not to move
somebody. All of it lives here until there is a person on the other side of it.

CONTACT - pulled out of the solo pages
Finish through a bump. Take the hit on the way up and let it change nothing about the finish.
Attack into contact, absorb it, counter off it into the finish. The counter is the point.
Navigate a screen with a real body in it - get skinny, take the hit, keep the line.
Hold your line while somebody rides your hip. Keep the path and keep the height.
Play through a bump on the catch before you shoot.
Post-up and seal work - anything where you move a body off a spot.

DEFENSE THAT NEEDS A PERSON
Deny work. You said you are open to this in a group.
Live one on one, full court and half court. The real version of everything on the Defense page.
Guarding a real screen where the screener actually screens.
Help and recover with a second offensive player who punishes a late closeout.
Post defense and guarding up a size.

PASSING AND READS THAT NEED A PERSON
Live-dribble passing where the help defender actually commits, so the read is real.
Two on one and three on two - the decision, not the delivery.
Off-ball cutting and screening timing, where arriving early or late actually costs something.

WHAT A PARTNER IS WORTH MOST FOR
Not more reps. Reps you can get alone. A partner is worth the things that cannot be faked:
a defender who reacts, contact that moves you, and a passer whose timing is not your own.
Spend partner time on those and nothing else."}]},"6":{"sel":1,"pages":[{"title":"Movement - Drive Position","body":"MOVEMENT - DRIVE POSITION
Every rep at stride height. Hips come up, the rep is over.

Low Stride Walk - 1x10, hold the bottom 2s
Low Stride Walk, no hold - 2x10
Low Drive Steps, half speed - 3x ea, 3 steps
Low Drive Steps, full speed - 4x ea, 3 steps
Low Drive to Low Stop - 4x ea, stop in 2 steps, hold 2s
Low Drive, Stop, Go back the other way - 3x ea
Low Drive to Cut - 3x ea, 45 degrees off the outside foot at the cone
Single-Leg Low Landing - 2x3 ea, from an angle, stick 2s

BUILD IT
Same ladder every day. The build is speed at the same height, then a stop, then a cut, then a call.
Stops - 2 steps until it is silent, then 1 step.
Cuts - sharper angle, later cut, then on a Split Second call (Left / Right).
Landings - further out, steeper angle.

FIRST SESSION OF THE MONTH
5-10-5 ___ s / ___ s

25-30 min, after the bag. Every rep at stance height. Hips come up, the rep is over.
Nothing here is scored on makes. Levels per drill. 2-3 drills a session.

1. LOW AND FAST                                               NOW: L___
Cover the lane low. Slide 3, open the hip and sprint 3, re-plant, slide 3. Stance height the whole way.
  L1  Game speed
  L2  Full speed, tape a mark at stance height, never above it
  L3  Slide 3, sprint 5, slide 3
  L4  Baseline to half court, low the whole way
  L5  Race the clock, Split Second Chase mode, beat your best time
  L6  Tired

2. STICK IT LOW                                               NOW: L___
Full speed into a one-leg stop, stuck in stance, 2 seconds, no wobble. Your own momentum is the contact.
  L1  Slide 3, stop on the outside foot
  L2  Sprint 3, stop on one foot in stance
  L3  Bound sideways into the one-leg stance, stick it
  L4  Land off balance on purpose, recover into stance, hold
  L5  Stick it, then push straight into the opposite direction
  L6  Which foot called late (Split Second Left / Right)
  L7  Tired

3. CLOSE AND CUT                                              NOW: L___
Full sprint at the cone, the shooter. Brake, cut 45 degrees to the spot, beat the drive there.
  L1  From 10 ft, stop in 2, cut to the spot
  L2  From the arc
  L3  Full sprint from half court
  L4  Cut called late as you arrive (Split Second Left / Right)
  L5  Spot further out, sharper cut
  L6  Stop in 1
  L7  Tired

4. PRESS TURN                                                 NOW: L___
Full court, low. Sprint 4 at an angle, cut, sprint 4 the other way. Turn the dribbler every cut.
  L1  Half court, 3 cuts, game speed
  L2  Full court, 5 cuts
  L3  Full speed, every cut off the outside foot
  L4  Cuts called late (Split Second Left / Right)
  L5  He beats you, cut into a re-plant and backpedal, then sprint again
  L6  Two lengths back to back
  L7  Tired

READS HALF - Split Second: On Ball, Ball Screen D, Transition D, Recover and Slide, Flip and Go, Chase.
Closeouts, slides, help, rotations - practice."},{"title":"DEFENSE READS - Split Second","body":"DEFENSE READS - SPLIT SECOND
All built and live in the app. Full spec: training-app/split-second-defense.json.
Section = the situation you already know. Call = what the offense shows you. Move on the countdown, find out as the call lands.

ON BALL - contain, beat him to the spot, hip to hip, no rise
  Left / Right / Cross / Hesi / Snatch / Blow by

BALL SCREEN D - say your coverage out loud before the rep
  Come off / Reject / Snake / Split / Pull up / Re-screen

TRANSITION D - sprint back, know who you have before you arrive
  Ball / Rim / Deepest / Match / Trailer

RECOVER AND SLIDE - slide, touch the floor, sprint back, go the way the call says
  Left / Right / Left back / Right back

FLIP AND GO - GO CUE mode. Slide in help, beep, flip the hips, sprint to the block or the backboard.
CHASE - GO CUE + STOPWATCH. Set up curl or flare, beep, chase it, tap to stop. Race your own best time.

Closeout D was cut - Recover and Slide covers it. The braking half is Closeout Stop on the Defense page."},{"title":"RECORDING - Does It Sell","body":"RECORDING - DOES IT SELL
Sun, Mon, Fri, Sat. 10-15 min, END of the workout, never cold.
Camera in FRONT of you at defender height. Tripod, slow-mo, tape the camera spot and your start spot.
3-4 moves, 3 reps each. About a dozen clips, all watched back.

Every clip gets one verdict:
SELLS - a frame where the defender has to commit wrong
DOESN'T SELL - nothing in it would have moved him
CAN'T TELL - too slow, or the camera was in the wrong place

One BEST REP clip per move. Beat it, replace it. Same angle every time.
Didn't sell = the move you work next session.

MOVES - your list, rotate through it

LOG - date, move, verdict"},{"title":"Film Protocol","body":"FILM PROTOCOL
First session of every month, before the session, fresh. Same time of day every month.
Tripod, never handheld. Slow-mo, 240fps if you have it. Landscape, full body, hip height.
Tape the camera spot and your start spot. Leave the tape.

THE SEQUENCE - always this order, no warm-up reps in the take
1. Split stance hold, side view - 10s ea
2. Low stride walk, side view - 4 strides
3. 3-step drive to 1-step stop, side view - 2 ea
4. Zig-zag drive stride, front view - 2 ea way
5. Closeout to 3 slides, baseline view - 2 ea
6. Single-leg landing from an angle, front view - 2 ea
7. Drive and kick pass, baseline view - 2 ea

One folder per month, named by date. Never delete one - the old months are the baseline.
Analysis is not built. Film anyway - it runs over old months later. Months you skip are gone.
